summary_en: This study compares siltuximab plus melphalan dosed by population pharmacokinetics (PK) with the usual melphalan dosing based on body surface area, in adults aged 60 or older with multiple myeloma who are having an autologous stem cell transplant. Siltuximab (11 mg/kg) is given 7 days before and 14 days after the stem cell infusion (plus or minus 2 days), and melphalan is infused over 30 minutes on Day -2. The record does not state a primary outcome measure; it says the study will compare how well the treatments work, look at symptoms after transplant, and study the safety of siltuximab. This is a Phase 2 randomized trial.
summary_es: Este estudio compara siltuximab más melfalán dosificado según la farmacocinética poblacional (PK) con la dosificación habitual de melfalán basada en la superficie corporal, en adultos de 60 años o más con mieloma múltiple que se someten a un trasplante autólogo de células madre. El siltuximab (11 mg/kg) se administra 7 días antes y 14 días después de la infusión de células madre (más o menos 2 días), y el melfalán se infunde durante 30 minutos el Día -2. El registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; señala que el estudio comparará qué tan bien funcionan los tratamientos, observará los síntomas después del trasplante y estudiará la seguridad del siltuximab. Es un ensayo aleatorizado de Fase 2.
who_for: Symptomatic multiple myeloma planned for autologous stem cell transplant with melphalan 140 or 200 mg/m2
At least 3 million CD34+ cells/kg available for infusion
Performance status: Karnofsky above 60% or ECOG 0-2
Organ function tests within 6 weeks before enrollment, including heart ejection fraction above 45% and adequate lung, blood count, liver and kidney values
not_for: Prior treatment with agents that target IL-6 or the IL-6 receptor
Other cancer within the past 2 years, with some skin and cervical cancer exceptions
Uncontrolled heart failure, uncontrolled arrhythmia, or QTc above 460 ms, or recent heart intervention
Clinically significant infection, including active hepatitis B or uncontrolled HIV or hepatitis C
Investigational drug use within 14 days, or live attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks of first study drug
